items.q: Maman plays hide-and-seek with her small son and finds him. Does 'Ej' sound like a happy surprise?
before: …sem izpod zavese na dvorišče. Maman je temnela. Kot tisti dan, ko je šla elektrika. Pogledal sem skozi luknjo v sredini zavese. Maman se je napolnila s svetlobo. Vlekla je nit iz nekega oblačila. Bila je tako dolga. Zasmejal sem se. Maman je dvignila glavo. Oči so ji postale velike. Rekla je:

items.text: Bravo, moj bistri deček. Ko te je česa strah, se domisli zvijače, da te ne bo več strah.
items.q: Maman praises her small son for a trick he uses against fear. Does this sound like a mother talking to a child?
before: Vedno sem uporabil zvijačo. Namesto na rdeča vrata sem gledal na steno hiše poleg nje. Bila je bela. Maman je rekla:

items.text: Ne. Dokler je ta nit v tvoji roki, se ne boš izgubil. Drugi konec je v moji roki.
items.q: Maman reassures her small son, who is afraid of getting lost. Does this sound like a mother talking to a child?

items.text: Ja, naš Baba-jan je zelo lačen spoštovanja.
items.q: Ghassem says sarcastically that their father hungers for respect. Does 'lačen spoštovanja' sound natural?

items.text: Ampak pristal je med napačnimi ljudmi – razbili smo mu še zadnjo trohico spoštovanja.
items.q: Ghassem jokes that their father landed among the wrong people, who smashed his last bit of respect. Does this sound natural?

items.text: Oooo. Ko bi le vedel, kaj se dogaja v glavi Nini-jan.
items.q: Ghassem lets out a long, fond sigh of delight at his mother's joke. Does 'Oooo' sound like that here?
before: – Ne, ne jemljite solz. Vzemite nasmehe.

items.text: Ooooo. Naj krožim okoli glavice Nini-jan, kako dobro dela.
items.q: Ghassem fondly teases his mother, whom the family call Nini, for her clever question. Does this sound affectionate and natural?
before: – Ghassem, pravim, ti ljudje, za katere Amir pravi, da tam v tujini ne verujejo dosti v boga, je tudi nje bog ustvaril?

items.text: Pri novoletni sofri, ko sem bral pesem za mamo, je Maman namesto da bi bila vesela postala zaskrbljena.
items.q: He read his poem to his mother at the very moment the year turned at Norouz. Does this line make that moment clear?

items.text: Ti samo pazi na hrano, za ostalo me ni briga.
items.q: Maman urges her grown son abroad to eat well above all. Does this sound like a caring mother?
before: – Mm-hm, tako je shujšala. Zadnjič, ko sem jo šla skopat, na telesu ni ostalo niti malo mesa — samo kost in koža. Pravim, če bi lahko jedla, ne bi prišlo do tega. Nana-pesar-jan, res moraš paziti, kaj ješ. Jej dobre stvari. Stvari, ki te krepijo.

items.text: Stari so vedno govorili, da besede nič ne stanejo — so samo vroč zrak.
items.q: Maman quotes an old saying that words cost nothing. Does it sound like a folk saying?
before: – Hmm, Ghassem govori samo zato, da bi se slišal.

items.text: Medtem je Mahboub jokala cel teden brez prestanka.
items.q: Maman recalls that back then her daughter cried for a whole week. Does 'Medtem' fit here?
Maman says a man had been drinking too much soda. Does 'gaziranega' sound natural on its own?

items.text: Išče si izgovore, da godrnja za prazen nič, hi-hi, Amir-jan.
items.q: Maman gives a short laugh while complaining about her husband. Does this sound like her?

items.text: Joj, Nini je naenkrat postala zaspana. Od jutra sem pokonci brez spanca.
items.q: Maman, calling herself Nini, the family's pet name for her, says she suddenly feels sleepy. Does this sound natural?
before: Maman močno stisne oči in reče:

items.text: Salaam, jigaram. Kako si? Si zdrav? Se dobro počutiš?
items.q: Maman greets her grown son warmly on a video call. Does this sound like a loving mother?

items.text: Tisti film z neumnim učiteljem? Mm-hm, glejte tega. Ta film je smešen, nasmeje te.
items.q: Maman tells the family which film to watch tonight. Does this sound like her everyday speech?
